attributes.additional_details: We believe hospitals should be legally required to complete robust safeguarding and discharge assessments before any vulnerable patient is discharged. These assessments should involve relevant family members, carers, social workers, community healthcare professionals, and safeguarding teams wherever appropriate, ensuring that decisions are made collaboratively and in the patient's best interests.
attributes.background: Too many vulnerable patients are being discharged from hospital without adequate assessments to ensure their safety, wellbeing, support arrangements, and ability to cope once they return home or move to another care setting.

rejection.details:
Under the Care Act 2014, NHS staff are already required to carry out assessments into vulnerable patients, including situations where it appears someone needs care and support.

You can read more about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/discharging-people-at-risk-of-or-experiencing-homelessness/discharging-people-at-risk-of-or-experiencing-homelessness#assessing-patients-for-safeguarding-and-care-needs
